mechanism_narrative: An increase in GDPC1 indicates strong economic growth, which should positively impact S&P 500 returns as corporate earnings are likely to improve.
failure_condition: If GDPC1 growth is positive but S&P 500 returns are negative over the 20-day horizon in more than 40% of cases.

mechanism_narrative: A rise in UNRATE suggests weakening labor market conditions, which could lead to negative S&P 500 returns as consumer spending may decline.
failure_condition: If UNRATE increases by more than 0.3pp but S&P 500 returns are positive in more than 50% of cases.

mechanism_narrative: When both UNRATE increases and PAYEMS decreases, it indicates a weakening labor market, leading to negative S&P 500 returns as economic growth slows.
failure_condition: If both UNRATE rises and PAYEMS falls but S&P 500 returns are positive in more than 40% of cases.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in FEDFUNDS indicates tighter monetary policy, which could lead to negative S&P 500 returns as borrowing costs increase and consumer spending decreases.
failure_condition: If FEDFUNDS exceeds 4.5% but S&P 500 returns are positive in more than 50% of cases.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in INDPRO suggests increased industrial production, which should positively impact S&P 500 returns as supply chains and manufacturing activity strengthen.
failure_condition: If INDPRO growth is positive but S&P 500 returns are negative over the 60-day horizon in more than 40% of cases.

mechanism_narrative: A decline in HOUST indicates reduced housing demand, which could lead to negative S&P 500 returns as the housing market, a key component of the economy, weakens.
failure_condition: If HOUST falls below 700 but S&P 500 returns are positive in more than 50% of cases.

mechanism_narrative: When CPIAUCSL increases and FEDFUNDS is high, it suggests inflationary pressures combined with tight monetary policy, leading to negative S&P 500 returns as real earnings decline.
failure_condition: If both CPIAUCSL increases and FEDFUNDS is high but S&P 500 returns are positive in more than 40% of cases.

mechanism_narrative: A low UNRATE in a strong economic regime suggests a robust labor market, leading to positive S&P 500 returns as consumer confidence and spending increase.
failure_condition: If UNRATE is low but S&P 500 returns are negative in more than 40% of cases.
